bullets.title: MU: Options volume hits $1.5B premium, market cap sheds $94B
bullets.body: MU options traded ~$1.5B in notional premium, exceeding SPY and QQQ combined (~$1B each). The stock lost ~$94B in market cap on the session, a move exceeding 1-standard-deviation for top-20 stocks; SpotGamma flags sector health at risk given the scale of the dislocation.

bullets.title: Semi sector under broad pressure: ARM -6%, MRVL/MU -4%, AVGO -2% pre-market
bullets.body: AVGO's soft guidance Wednesday night triggered AI-sector selling; pre-market had ARM -6%, MRVL/MU -4%, SNDK -2%, AVGO -2%, NVDA -1.9%, INTC -3.8%, CIEN -3.7%, LITE -4.6%, CRDO -3.8%. GS notes SOX closed ~75% above its 200-dma Wednesday, the most extended since 1999-2000. Korea's KOSPI fell ~5.5% overnight with SK Hynix -10%.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen certifies MU/Samsung/SK Hynix as HBM4 suppliers; AMD EPYC in switch trays
bullets.body: Jensen Huang formally certified Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix as qualified HBM4 memory suppliers for Nvidia's next-generation chips. Separately, NVIDIA uses AMD EPYC processors in its switch trays rather than Intel hardware.

bullets.title: TSLA: JPMorgan upgrades to Neutral from Underweight, raises PT to $475 from $145
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded Tesla from Underweight to Neutral and lifted its price target to $475 from $145, shifting the thesis to autonomous driving, robotics, AI, and software optionality rather than near-term EV earnings.

bullets.title: Jefferies CoWoS upgrade: TSM, NVDA, AVGO PTs raised; supply gap widens to 15-20%
bullets.body: Jefferies raises CoWoS forecasts to 180k wpm by end-2027E (from 170k) and 220k by end-2028E. NVDA maintains 50%+ allocation; AVBO revised down to 24-25% (from 28.5%) but TPU volumes robust at 6.2mn. TSM supply-demand gap widens to 15-20% with 10%+ wafer ASP increases for all customers in 2027E. AAPL to pay only 1-2% more in 2026E but 10%+ in 2027E.

bullets.title: AVGO: soft guidance sparks sector selloff; AI infrastructure visibility extending past CY27
bullets.body: Broadcom's Wednesday guidance missed expectations and catalyzed broad premarket selling across the semiconductor complex. GS notes that AVGO management commentary on AI infrastructure visibility extending beyond CY27 was a positive signal buried beneath the headline miss. Semis rallied ~5% intraday Thursday prior to the guidance release.

bullets.title: ORCL/ADBE: Next week's key earnings; ORCL $25B equity raise and FY27 CapEx guide in focus
bullets.body: Oracle reports Wednesday after close with consensus FY27 CapEx at $61.2B (~22% y/y), plus updates on its $25B equity raise. Adobe reports Thursday after close. Both are primary catalysts for the software complex next week.

bullets.title: AAPL WWDC Monday: AI/Siri expectations high; App Store growth decelerating to 8% YoY
bullets.body: Apple's WWDC kicks off Monday in Cupertino with the Street focused on AI/Siri announcements. Apple's App Store ecosystem grew only 8% to $1.4T in 2025 vs. 18% prior, signaling services deceleration and monopoly headwinds. Apple is increasingly dependent on third parties (Google Cloud, Nvidia) for frontier AI, suggesting either a frontier model gap or commoditization thesis. Apple Neo captured ~18% of 1Q26 MacBook shipments in a 3-week window at the $599 price tier.

bullets.title: SNOW: Oppenheimer reiterates Outperform, $295 PT after Summit; 60% of customers expect >20% spend growth
bullets.body: Post Snowflake Summit, Oppenheimer maintains Outperform with $295 PT. 60% of customers expect >20% YoY spending growth; 75% increasing Cortex Code use. Snowflake's competitive edge framed as production-grade governed agentic AI at scale. FY27E revenue $6.1B, FY28E $7.4B.

bullets.title: GWRE: ARR miss on deal slippage sends stock -12%; 88% buy ratings intact
bullets.body: Guidewire fell ~12% below its 50-dma after Q3 deal pushouts caused an ARR miss (in-line at $1.15B) despite revenue +26.9% y/y beating by 4.7%. Average analyst target cut 8.1% to $207.92 (Citizens to $220, Goldman to $225, RBC to $215, Stifel to $200). GS views the fully-ramped ARR as a positive signal for F4Q conversion.

bullets.title: CSCO: KeyBanc raises to Overweight, $125 PT; Cisco Live highlights AI platform positioning
bullets.body: KeyBanc upgrades Cisco to Overweight with a $125 PT (~19.5x FY27 adj. EBITDA) after Cisco Live, citing the Cloud Control AI-native unified platform, end-of-life Cat 4K/6K refresh cycle, and security leadership. Cisco is a charter member of Anthropic's Glasswing and OpenAI's Daybreak programs; 400G→800G→1.6T optics transition underway.

bullets.title: META: Mizuho sizes click-to-messenger ads at $40B in 2026 (~16% of ad revs), growing 40% YoY
bullets.body: Mizuho estimates Meta's click-to-messenger ad format reached $40B in 2026 revenue (vs $10B+ disclosed in 2023), growing at 40% YoY and contributing ~4% to overall growth. AI Agents could make messenger revenue surpass ad revenue within a decade.

bullets.title: DELL: First Vera Rubin NVL72 systems shipped to CoreWeave; claims 10x lower cost-per-token vs Blackwell
bullets.body: Dell shipped its first Vera Rubin NVL72 AI server systems to CoreWeave and claims 10x lower cost-per-token vs Blackwell for agentic inference workloads. SMCI secured a ~$2B supply deal with Gorilla Technology for India's Yotta project (20,736 B300 + 5,120 B200 cards). Pre-market: DELL -3.8%, SMCI broadly lower.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Data center structural deficit at 12 GW; incumbents advantaged on siting/power
bullets.body: Jefferies estimates ~21 GW of 2025 data center demand vs <9 GW delivered, widening the deficit to 12 GW. Hyperscaler capex surges to $770B in 2026E (+74% YoY). EQIX and DLR report no siting issues due to smaller facilities and operational experience, with vacancy at 1-3% in primary markets. Switch private fundraise values company at $50B+, a materially higher multiple than public DC REITs.

bullets.title: TXN earnings catalyst spurs analog semi buying; infrastructure software seeing net buying flows
bullets.body: Jefferies flow desk notes TXN's upside earnings and above-seasonal guidance drove broad net buying in analog semis. Infrastructure software seeing net buying among both hedge funds and long-only investors after 9 straight weeks of Software net selling in early 2025. Memory stocks also showing strong net buying momentum. Hardware seeing broad-based net buying across client types.

bullets.title: DELL/MU flagged in bubble territory; SOX most overbought since 1999-2000
bullets.body: 22V Research and a multi-strategy webinar both flag bubble price action in select stocks including Dell and Micron, with SOX most overbought since 1999-2000. Three-month implied correlations at 5-year lows leave short index vol positions vulnerable. Separately, 22V maintains Bitcoin target of 40k and expects MSTR/COIN to work materially lower.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Morgan Stanley upgrades on monetization momentum, China optionality, Vector product
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades Unity to Buy in its SMID-cap daily, citing runtime data monetization, accelerating Create segment, Unity AI/Vector synergies, and China optionality. Competitive risk viewed as lower than feared. MS separately calls U a multi-year growth driver.

bullets.title: T/VZ/CMCSA/CHTR: Wolfe flags Starlink as existential threat; sector down -13 to -27% YTD
bullets.body: Wolfe Research warns Starlink could serve ~40% of US households in broadband by 2030 with V3 satellites + Starship providing ~22x capacity per rocket. Big 3 MNOs have publicly refused MVNO deals but cost/benefit may shift. Telecom sub-sector down -13.2% YTD vs S&P +10.8%; cable down -27.4%. SpaceX IPO is a rising overhang for the entire sector.

bullets.title: INTU at 52-week low, down 61% YTD; Foxconn May revenue +39.6% YoY (bullish AAPL/NVDA supply chain)
bullets.body: StreetAccount flags Intuit at a 52-week low, down 61% YTD. On a positive supply-chain read-through, Foxconn reported May revenue up 39.6% YoY to NT$859.4B (~$27.3B), its 3rd best month ever, with Q2 tracking 'well above previously anticipated significant growth' on AI servers and iPhone assembly.

bullets.title: ABNB: Jefferies bullish on TAM expansion from hotels, Experiences, services buildout
bullets.body: Jefferies highlights Airbnb's product expansion into hotels, Experiences, and adjacent services as supporting sustained double-digit revenue growth and long-term upside. BKNG and EXPE noted in Hedgeye's coverage but no specific directional view extracted for those names.
